disclaimer: Agave genomics is less developed than grass crops. The A. tequilana genome was published in 2019 (Abraham et al.); A. deserti partial sequence also available. Many entries use CAM plant model systems (Kalanchoë, Crassula) or Agave-specific transcriptomic studies. CAM pathway genes are especially well-supported.

evidenceLevelKey.Peer-Reviewed Literature: Gene directly characterized in Agave spp. in a published peer-reviewed study.
evidenceLevelKey.Curated Database Reference: Gene annotated in a curated database for Agave or well-supported CAM plant ortholog.
evidenceLevelKey.Homology-Based Projection: Gene inferred from a characterized ortholog in Kalanchoë, Mesembryanthemum crystallinum, Arabidopsis, or a sequenced Agave genome.
evidenceLevelKey.Environment-Relevance Estimate: Pathway relevance inferred from Agave physiology and Texas arid-land environment.

genes.name: CAM-type phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase (nocturnal CO2 fixation)
genes.functionSummary: The defining enzyme of CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism) photosynthesis. Agave opens stomata at night, capturing CO2 using PEPC to form malate (C4 acid), which is stored in vacuoles. During the day, stomata close — preventing water loss — and malate is decarboxylated to release CO2 for Rubisco. This gives Agave exceptionally high water-use efficiency (~1/10th of C3 crops per gram of biomass).
genes.orthologSource: Agave tequilana CAM-PEPC; Abraham PE et al. 2016 Sci Rep 6:38303; Borland AM et al. 2014 Plant Cell 26(7):2634–2654
genes.limitationNote: CAM PEPC is among the best-characterized Agave genes. Diel regulation (phosphorylation at night, inactivation by day) is well-documented.

genes.name: PEP carboxylase kinase (CAM regulation)
genes.functionSummary: Phosphorylates and activates CAM-PEPC at night. PPCK expression is controlled by the circadian clock — transcript peaks in the early night, activating PEPC for nocturnal CO2 uptake. Inactivation of PPCK during the day prevents futile carbon recycling. A molecular clock output gene unique to CAM plants.
genes.orthologSource: Agave PPCK; Hartwell J et al. 1999 Plant J 20(3):333–342; Boxall SF et al. 2017 New Phytol 214(4):1469–1480 (Kalanchoë model)
genes.limitationNote: PPCK circadian regulation is an elegant feature of CAM; well-studied in Kalanchoë and directly supported in Agave transcriptomics.

genes.name: Malate dehydrogenase (CAM malate storage)
genes.functionSummary: Reduces oxaloacetate (from PEPC reaction) to malate in the cytoplasm at night. The malate is transported into the central vacuole for overnight storage. At dawn, vacuolar malate is exported and decarboxylated (by NADP-ME or PCK) to release CO2 for daytime Rubisco fixation behind closed stomata.
genes.orthologSource: Agave MDH; Abraham PE et al. 2016 Sci Rep 6:38303; Bohnert HJ, Cushman JC 2000 Curr Opin Plant Biol 3(3):231–238
genes.limitationNote: MDH is a central CAM gene — the stoichiometry of malate accumulation per CO2 fixed is a key bioenergy efficiency parameter.

genes.name: Aluminum-activated malate transporter (vacuolar malate uptake)
genes.functionSummary: Transports malate into the central vacuole at night, allowing overnight storage without acidifying the cytoplasm. Vacuolar malate capacity per cell determines how much CO2 an Agave leaf can fix nocturnally — a key bottleneck in CAM carbon storage efficiency.
genes.orthologSource: Arabidopsis AtALMT9 vacuolar malate transporter (AT3G18440); De Angeli A et al. 2013 Nature 497(7450):468–472; Kalanchoë TDT ortholog
genes.limitationNote: Vacuolar malate transport is well-characterized in Kalanchoë and Mesembryanthemum; Agave-specific transporter identity needs confirmation.

genes.name: NADP-malic enzyme (daytime CO2 release for Rubisco)
genes.functionSummary: Decarboxylates malate in the chloroplast during the day, releasing CO2 directly to Rubisco behind closed stomata. This creates a CO2 concentrating effect analogous to C4 photosynthesis but with a temporal separation rather than spatial. NADP-ME activity during Phase III of CAM is the primary CO2 source for daytime carbon fixation in Agave.
genes.orthologSource: Agave NADP-ME; Cushman JC et al. 2008 Plant Cell Environ 31(2):215–222; Dever LV et al. 1998 J Exp Bot 49(321):845–854
genes.limitationNote: NADP-ME and/or PCK (PEP carboxykinase) can serve as the decarboxylating enzyme in different CAM plants.

genes.name: FLOWERING LOCUS T / FUL-like (monocarpic flowering)
genes.functionSummary: Controls flowering initiation in Agave. Agave plants are monocarpic — they flower once, produce seed, and die. After 8–30 years of vegetative growth, the plant bolts, producing a massive inflorescence stalk. This monocarpic trait is controlled by FT/FUL-related genes responding to temperature and age cues. Managing flowering time is key to maximizing vegetative biomass for bioenergy.
genes.orthologSource: Agave FT-related; Ávila de Dios E et al. 2019 BMC Genomics 20:928; Arabidopsis AtFUL (AT5G60910)
genes.limitationNote: Monocarpy is an important agronomic trait — identifying and managing FT expression could enable longer-lived high-yield Agave bioenergy varieties.

genes.name: Fructosyltransferase / Sucrose:sucrose 1-fructosyltransferase (fructan biosynthesis)
genes.functionSummary: Catalyzes the biosynthesis of fructans (agavins) from sucrose in Agave storage tissue (piña). Agavins are branched fructopolysaccharides unique to Agave — the primary fermentable carbohydrate for tequila and bioethanol. High fructosyltransferase activity corresponds to high fructan accumulation in the mature piña (the harvested storage organ).
genes.orthologSource: Agave tequilana SST/FFT enzymes; Mancilla-Margalli NA, López MG 2006 J Agric Food Chem 54(26):9892–9902; Valluru R, Van den Ende W 2008 J Exp Bot 59(11):2905–2916
genes.limitationNote: Fructan structure and composition are well-characterized for A. tequilana (tequila production) and directly relevant to bioenergy.

genes.name: Invertase (sucrose hydrolysis for fermentation pre-processing)
genes.functionSummary: Hydrolyzes sucrose to glucose + fructose, and assists in fructan hydrolysis during juice extraction. Acid invertases in the piña cell wall release fermentable hexoses during the cooking/hydrolysis step of ethanol production. Controls the available fermentable sugar pool.
genes.orthologSource: Agave invertase; Bernal LM et al. 2008 J Plant Physiol 165(2):211–221; Mancilla-Margalli NA, López MG 2006
genes.limitationNote: Invertase and inulinase activities in Agave piña are commercially relevant and well-characterized in tequila production literature.

genes.name: Group 3 LEA dehydrin (extreme drought protection)
genes.functionSummary: Late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) dehydrin proteins protect cellular structures during extreme desiccation. Agave can survive soil moisture levels that would kill most other plants. These dehydrins function as molecular shields preventing protein aggregation and membrane disruption during severe water deficit — key to Agave's unique survival in arid West Texas environments.
genes.orthologSource: Agave dehydrin; Cushman JC, Bohnert HJ 2000 Curr Opin Plant Biol 3(2):117–124; Abraham PE et al. 2016 Sci Rep 6:38303
genes.limitationNote: Extreme desiccation tolerance in Agave is physiologically documented; specific LEA gene identities need genomic confirmation.

genes.name: Rubisco large subunit (daytime carbon fixation)
genes.functionSummary: Large catalytic subunit of Rubisco; fixes CO2 released from stored malate during the day in CAM plants. Unlike C3 plants where Rubisco is constrained by photorespiration in hot dry conditions, CAM plants provide concentrated CO2 from malate to Rubisco behind closed stomata, allowing efficient carbon fixation while conserving water.
genes.orthologSource: Agave rbcL chloroplast gene; Abraham PE et al. 2016 Sci Rep 6:38303; standard CAM model
genes.limitationNote: Rubisco large subunit is chloroplast-encoded in all plants; Agave rbcL sequences are available in GenBank.

genes.name: Copper/zinc superoxide dismutase (ROS defense — arid stress)
genes.functionSummary: Cytoplasmic CuZn-SOD converts superoxide radicals to hydrogen peroxide under heat and drought stress. Agave plants regularly experience intense solar radiation and heat — conditions that generate high ROS levels in leaves. Efficient ROS detoxification is part of Agave's remarkable tolerance to the extremes of the Texas desert climate.
genes.orthologSource: Agave SOD (transcriptomic support); Abraham PE et al. 2016 Sci Rep 6:38303; Gill SS, Tuteja N 2010 Plant Physiol Biochem 48(12):909–930
genes.limitationNote: SOD upregulation under heat/drought stress is broadly documented in succulents; Agave-specific protein characterization is limited.

genes.name: Cation/H+ antiporter (vacuolar acidification in CAM)
genes.functionSummary: V-type H+-ATPases and CAX (cation/H+ antiporters) at the tonoplast membrane acidify the vacuole at night to drive malate2- uptake against a proton gradient. Vacuolar pH drops from ~5.5 to ~3.5 overnight in Agave leaves — a massive acid accumulation reflecting the scale of CAM CO2 fixation.
genes.orthologSource: Arabidopsis AtCAX1 (AT2G38170); Mesembryanthemum VHA-a ortholog; Lüttge U 2000 Prog Bot 61:261–286
genes.limitationNote: Vacuolar acidification mechanism is physiologically well-documented in Agave; specific transporter protein identity at gene level needs Agave genomic confirmation.
